closureMeaning: The redesigned Wave 3 implementation work is closed. Capabilities marked complete or complete-with-boundary are implemented for their declared scope. Partial and deferred items are not represented as complete and require a future explicitly scoped workstream if they are resumed.

statusDefinitions.complete: Implemented and validated for the redesigned Wave 3 scope with no known in-scope product gap.
statusDefinitions.complete-with-boundary: Implemented and validated for the declared scope, with an explicit source, coverage, maturity, automation or execution boundary that must remain visible.
statusDefinitions.partial: A useful implementation exists, but a known in-scope presentation or workflow gap remains.
statusDefinitions.deferred: Intentionally not implemented in Wave 3; the reason and restart condition are explicit.
statusDefinitions.replaced: A legacy capability was intentionally superseded by a different redesigned capability.

evidence: Place Registry schema, data layer, selectors and integrity audit are implemented.
Current integrity snapshot contains 88 unique records, 23 canonical Makati barangays, no duplicate IDs or exact duplicate coordinates, and generated civic-entity-index parity.
Registry relationships and provenance are guarded by scripts/audit-place-registry-integrity.mjs.
capabilities.boundary: The registry is complete for the verified/current named scope established by the Wave 3 source-reconciliation work, not a claim that every possible Makati place, street segment or facility has been mapped.

evidence: Canonical places are reused in BetterBarangay, Mobility, Services/Government Offices and Saan Ako Lalapit.
Global Search indexes Place Registry records.
Visit Makati and Heritage reuse exact canonical place links where identity is unambiguous.
Projects/Accountability and City Monitor expose explicit place relationships without fuzzy matching.
A reusable Near me selector/component consumes Place Registry coordinates.

capabilities.capability: Task-led Civic Map and place-detail experience
evidence: Civic Map is registry-first and separates place, segment and route entities.
Primary jobs are finding a civic record, reporting a problem, suggesting an improvement and recording current conditions.
Place detail pages separate canonical facts, structured observations, community cases, proposals and explicit related public records.
Generic star-rating/review framing is retired from redesigned surfaces.

capabilities.capability: Nearby public-realm reporting and canonical matching
evidence: Users can use device location, registry search or manual coordinates.
Nearby results are suggestions only; server-side submission re-normalizes entity identity from the canonical index.
Location-only reports remain possible when no canonical entity matches.
Duplicate open cases are detected by entity/category/proximity and can be confirmed instead of duplicated.
Emergency categories are rejected from normal Civic Map submission and routed to 911.

capabilities.capability: Evidence-separated civic case lifecycle and referral tracking
evidence: Lifecycle states remain distinct: reviewed, forwarded, acknowledged, action-reported and community-verified-resolved.
Community confirmations and appears-resolved signals remain separate from official lifecycle evidence.
Authority, channel, external reference and timestamp fields are preserved in machine-readable admin events and public case readback.
W3R-10 instrumentation exposes first-stage timestamps, elapsed-hours inputs and evidence diagnostics.
capabilities.boundary: Automatic government forwarding is intentionally deferred. Forwarded means BetterMakati documented a referral attempt; it does not prove authority acknowledgement.

evidence: Five observation families and canonical question sets are implemented.
Observation submission validates canonical entity/category/family/question-set compatibility.
Observations use observedAt and remain separate from complaints, cases and canonical registry facts.
Observation readback includes freshness inputs and sample-aware summaries without composite scores.

capabilities.capability: Bounded civic audit campaigns and live output
evidence: A reusable civic-audit campaign schema and workflow are defined.
The 2026 public-park accessibility pilot freezes 13 verified public-park targets and four directly observable questions.
Live results preserve zero-observation targets, sample counts, question distributions, campaign period and data-availability state.
Coverage outputs use raw numerator/denominator inputs and do not derive park scores or rankings.

capabilities.capability: Participation Hub and Get Involved task routing
evidence: Participation exposes official participation, local problem reporting, place improvements, condition observations, corrections, sources, ideas and volunteering from one task-led entry.
Get Involved supports proposal, idea, source, correction, volunteer and contact submissions with native tracking, duplicate handling and a pre-filled fallback.
Fallback-created issues now use the same metadata format as native submissions so later duplicate detection remains continuous.
Barangay query context is resolved to the canonical barangay name and carried into general submissions.
capabilities.boundary: No complete authoritative citywide consultation calendar has been identified. The official-opportunity section therefore keeps an honest empty state and official Makati events handoff rather than fabricating completeness.

evidence: Barangay scope is preserved into Civic Map and nearby reporting.
Barangay contribution links carry barangay context into Get Involved.
Barangay pages expose local civic records and participation actions without requiring a separate barangay-only backend.
Activity presentation is tied to actual canonical/local evidence rather than an invented completeness score.

capabilities.capability: Outcome metric definitions, publication guardrails and raw instrumentation
evidence: Case outcome definitions cover review, routing, acknowledgement, action evidence and documented resolution plus elapsed-time inputs.
Observation freshness and civic-audit coverage definitions are explicit.
Publication thresholds require minimum case/event counts and cohort maturity before lifecycle rates or medians can be public.
API/data instrumentation exposes raw per-case, freshness and audit metric inputs without adding headline rates.
capabilities.boundary: Threshold-gated public lifecycle rates, timing medians and aggregate freshness rates are not published until their sample, maturity and inventory requirements are met.

evidence: Metric semantics and privacy requirements are defined.
Current anonymous contribution data has no privacy-safe stable contributor key.
capabilities.reason: Do not infer identity from IP address, public alias or free-text name. Resume only after a pseudonymous non-public contributor key, retention/deletion rules and explicit instrumentation design exist.

evidence: Civic Reports correctly separates evidence status, community resolution signals and referral candidates.
The six-stage lifecycle wording is present.
W3R-10 raw outcome instrumentation exists.
capabilities.gap: The public reports page is still dominated by legacy seven-day/thirty-day volume counts and a three-support proposal threshold. It does not yet present the redesigned outcome model with W3R-10b threshold suppression.
capabilities.restartCondition: Create a separate follow-up workstream to redesign /civic-map/reports around threshold-gated outcome evidence while retaining exact recent-case records and referral workflow. Do not publish lifecycle rates or medians before thresholds are met.

capabilities.capability: Participation QA and integrity regression coverage
evidence: Human/source-level audit covers Participation, Get Involved, Civic Map, nearby reporting, entity detail, reports and civic-audit surfaces.
Place Registry integrity audit guards identity, barangays, coordinates, lifecycle/provenance and relationships.
General participation handler tests cover submission, duplicate, fallback, tracking and barangay context.
Public-place handler tests cover canonical matching, duplicate confirmation, lifecycle evidence, observations and civic-audit aggregation.
Wave 3 accessibility regression audit guards mobile width locks, minimum touch targets, focus, reduced motion, async state semantics and hidden honeypots.
Source-level responsive/accessibility review and deterministic handler-level journey suites are committed and wired into build/quality scripts.
capabilities.boundary: No GitHub Actions run or browser/device automation result was available during W3R-11c through W3R-11e. Wave 3 therefore does not claim independently executed CI, physical-device or screen-reader validation.

replacedLegacyPatterns.legacy: Civic Map-owned asset model as the only home of place identity
replacedLegacyPatterns.replacement: Shared canonical Place Registry reused across the website.

replacedLegacyPatterns.legacy: Generic rating/review workflow and star-style public-realm scoring
replacedLegacyPatterns.replacement: Structured dated condition observations and bounded civic audits with sample counts.

replacedLegacyPatterns.legacy: Participation feedback loop led primarily by recent volume/popularity counts
replacedLegacyPatterns.replacement: Defined outcome evidence: review, routing, acknowledgement, action, documented resolution, freshness and audit coverage, with public-threshold guardrails.

explicitDeferrals.reason: Destination, authorization, evidence and accountability rules are not yet reliable enough for automated government delivery.
No sufficiently authoritative complete current citywide consultation calendar has been identified.
No privacy-safe stable contributor identity exists; IP address and public aliases are explicitly prohibited as substitutes.
Publication requires the W3R-10b minimum denominator/event counts and stage-specific cohort maturity.
Publication requires an explicit eligible inventory of at least 10 entities, at least 5 observed entities and the family-specific freshness window.
The human audit found /civic-map/reports still volume-heavy. This is the one known redesigned participation presentation gap and is not classified complete.
No browser/device automation or GitHub Actions execution evidence was available in the current environment.
Unresolved exact facility/park/linear-infrastructure items remain governed by the source-reconciliation and completeness-audit files rather than being silently treated as mapped.

closureDecision.why: All 38 planned redesign micro-steps are complete after W3R-11f, but one public feedback-loop presentation capability remains partial and several explicitly bounded capabilities remain deferred or threshold-gated.
whatMayBeCalledComplete: Place Registry foundation and cross-site reuse for the declared verified scope.
Task-led reporting, structured observations, civic audit pilot, redesigned participation routing and data/API outcome instrumentation.
whatMustNotBeCalledComplete: A complete authoritative citywide consultation calendar.
Public lifecycle outcome rates/medians before thresholds are met.
Physical-device/screen-reader or independently executed CI validation.
